esc-inclusive-education-support-kampala-.about:
Kampala School for the Physically Handicapped (KSPH) is a Ugandan primary school for children with physical disabilities, founded in 1968 by parents of children with cerebral palsy. Its aim is to educate, rehabilitate, and equip learners for self-reliance and development. The school follows the national curriculum and offers sports, music, dance, drama, spiritual fellowship, and education tours. It also provides vocational training in tailoring, screen printing, crafts, tie and dye, and basic computer skills for children who cannot continue to further education. KSPH has 100 pupils aged 6–18 with disabilities such as cerebral palsy, muscular dystrophy, spina bifida, and polio. It has 13 teachers, 5 trained in special needs education, including 2 disabled former students. Volunteers support classroom learning, extracurriculars, wheelchair repair (voluntary), therapy exercises, teacher training, fundraising, and basic computer teaching.

esc-laulasmaa-school-laulasmaa-2027.about:
Laulasmaa is a village in Northern Estonia on the shore of Lahepere Bay and is 29 km away from the capital. Laulasmaa School is an organisation which is made up of three schools and three kindergartens at Laulasmaa, Klooga and Lehola. The school and the kindergarten at Laulasmaa are the biggest. It has 280 pupils and 85 employees, and provides primary education. The kindergarten has 126 children from the age of 1-6. Laulasmaa School maintains and develops Estonian culture by paying attention to Estonian language and the study of culture. In addition to the traditional subjects, the students learn folklore, crafts, art, folk dances, choir songs, music. Also, the children take part in hobby classes, contests and other projects. Laulasmaa School knows that non-formal learning is important. During breaks, the school offers the children a variety of activities. More information and how to apply:

Accommodation will typically be in a shared apartment or hostel, furnished with essential items. Rooms may be private or shared, depending on availability, with shared kitchen and bathroom facilities. Volunteers receive €5/day pocket money and additional food allowance per month, managing their own meals. International travel is reimbursed based on set travel budget and task related local transport is covered to full extent. Volunteers will take part in the ESC training cycle organized by the Estonian National Agency, which focuses on personal development and intercultural learning. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Do you want to help nature get healthy again? We are a non-profit organisation dedicated to create and maintain an eco-friendly way of agriculture. Our gardeners will teach you skills about the nature-friendly production of organic vegetables and fruits, soil regeneration, and nature conservation. Our site is beautifully situated beneath the Eco-Village "Lebensgarten Steyerberg". Enjoy new experiences together with other international volunteers. You will learn a lot about organic gardening and permaculture and dive deeper into innovative practices of creating healthy soil on an organic farm that is certified under the international biocyclic vegan standard. You can take part in seminars and other activities that will help you to develop your personality and you can make new like minded friends.
